title: Sample drift sleuth - late-night scratchpad
content:
Context:
Late-night exploratory notes after noticing a spike in "output-oddity" alerts for redwood-hosted model redwood-v1 (hosted:us-west-2). Alert linked INF-2345. Quick check: traffic pattern unchanged, but regression window starts ~2024-10-21 03:00 UTC (rolling deploy?).

Goal:
- Rapidly triage whether this is: prompt-distribution drift, model-side regression (weights/serving change), decoder sampling bug, or post-processing change (tokenizer/normalizer).
- Produce an ad-hoc rubric for quick sampling and signal extraction we can run across 500 random samples and 50 seed prompts.

Quick observations (first-pass):
- Many previously correct completions now include terse numeric prefixes ("1.", "2.") where not prompted. Feels like a subtle template injection or decoding temperature effect.
- Affected across chat and plain completion routes, more visible on streaming responses.
- Not obviously hallucination — content still relevant but format changed. Might break downstream parsing.

Seed prompts to repro (copy these into /eval/seed-prompts later):
1) "Summarize the policy in two sentences."
2) "Extract the main steps from the following instructions:
   - Preheat oven..."
3) "Give me three bullet points on the benefits of using caching in inference."
4) "Write a one-paragraph product blurb for a developer tool named "Pinch"."

Example outputs sampled 2024-10-22 01:15 UTC (redwood-v1):
PROMPT 1 -> redwood-v1 (expected: paragraph):
  "We help teams ship model features faster and with less operational overhead." (expected)
  Observed: "1. We help teams ship model features faster and with less operational overhead."

PROMPT 3 -> redwood-v1 (expected bullets):
  Observed: "1) Lower latency per request
2) More efficient GPU utilization" (previously: "- Lower latency per request
- More efficient GPU utilization")

Immediate hypotheses:
- A rerun of a prompt-formatting normalization (strip/munge) PR accidentally toggled list-tokenization or added ordinalization. Check PR 987 (serving-runtime) for tokenizer changes.
- Sampling/temperature or top-k defaults changed in the deployment config causing the model to prefer numbered list tokens.
- Downstream post-processing (server-side response normalizer) now runs a light "structureify" pass that converts plain dashes into ordered lists when it sees common list patterns.

Ad-hoc rubric (compact) - quick human check for 50 samples: (scale 0-2 where 0 = regression, 1 = partial, 2 = OK)
- Format fidelity (expected vs observed format): 0/1/2
- Semantic fidelity (information preserved): 0/1/2
- Parse safety (will downstream parser break?): 0/1/2
- Regression severity (user-impact): 0/1/2
- Signal weight (how many similar samples in batch): 0/1/2

Scoring guide (notes):
- Format fidelity 0 = wrong list structure inserted (e.g., numbered when bullets expected) or extraneous tokens at start; 1 = minor punctuation shift; 2 = identical format.
- Semantic fidelity: 2 if no semantic loss; 1 if missing minor detail; 0 if factually wrong.

Quick triage steps (what I did / next steps):
- grep logs for "^1\." pattern in responses around 2024-10-21..22 (found higher incidence post-deploy).
- compared model config snapshot for redwood-v1 between 2024-10-20 and 2024-10-21 (weights unchanged, but serving-config shows temperature default changed from 0.0 -> 0.2 on the canary group). Pinged SRE.
- inspected PR 987: includes a fix for streaming JSON escaping; one commit touches response_postprocess/structureify.py (added feature flag).

Preliminary verdict: probable server-side postprocess flag accidentally enabled for some users; interacts with non-zero temperature to produce numeric list tokens. Combo effect leads to brittle formatted outputs.

Minimal reproducible test to run (automated):
- Run batch of 200 seed prompts across two endpoints: redwood-v1@stable (config temp=0.0) and redwood-v1@canary (temp=0.2 + structureify flag on). Compare count of numeric-prefix outputs.
- Command (pseudo): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","prompt":"<seed>","temperature":0.0}' and same with temp=0.2 and structureify toggle. Collate results with small parser that counts leading ^\s*[0-9]+[\.\)] tokens.

Data capture plan:
- For each sample store: prompt_id, prompt_hash, endpoint_tag, model_version, config_snapshot_id, raw_response, normalized_tokens (first 40 tokens).
- Tag samples where format changed but semantics preserved so we can decide tolerance thresholds.

Notes to self / open questions:
- If structureify is behind feature flag, who toggled it? Search Slack channel #deploys and audit logs for feature-flag changes 2024-10-20..21.
- Does this affect embeddings? Unlikely but check embedding pipeline for pre-tokenization differences.
- If we need a fast rollback, disabling the postprocess flag is lower risk than changing temperature defaults.

Proposed quick actions (owner / ETA):
- @Marta Ruiz: run the batch job across canary/stable and paste results in INF-2345 (ETA: 3h).
- @Noah Simons: check feature-flag audit (ETA: 1h) and confirm who toggled structureify.
- Me (Avery): draft a short mitigation playbook for CS to update customers if rollback necessary (ETA: today EOD).

Checklist before closing this scratchpad:
- [ ] Run automated sample job and upload CSV to INF-2345
- [ ] Add 50 curated customer-facing prompts to ensure no false positives
- [ ] Confirm if any downstream parsers changed in the same window
- [ ] Create follow-up task: evaluate if we should add format-regression alert rule (e.g., numeric-list-insertion-rate > 2% per 1k samples)

Quick log snippets (copied):
- found matching response: "1. Implement caching to reduce repeated work." (resp id: resp-20241021-7af3)
- feature flag event: ff-toggle: structureify=true by user: deploy-bot at 2024-10-21T02:47:12Z

Endnotes (scratch):
- Keep this doc lean. Once we have batch results move to confluence page under EVAL/format-regressions and staple the CSV.
- Save a couple of odd outputs as examples for docs and CS templates.

-- Avery
